problem: Leadership argued it was easier to learn and collaborate in person.
title: Amazon requires corporate staff in the office five days a week
context: CEO Andy Jassy announced in September 2024 that employees would return to the office five days a week from January 2025.
decision_made: Move from three to five office days a week, with exceptions for intensive coding work or a sick child with manager consent.
action_taken: Offered commuter benefits and subsidised parking; the company denied it was a backdoor layoff.
observed_outcome: Employee reaction was largely negative, including a remote-work Slack channel with more than 30,000 members and reports of people applying elsewhere. AWS's CEO said nine in ten employees he spoke with were excited.
lessons: Return-to-office mandates can produce strong immediate backlash, and leaders and staff may report very different sentiment.
limitations: Mostly Fortune coverage from September to November 2024. Effects on attrition or productivity were not found.

claims.claim_text: Amazon told employees to return to the office five days a week from January 2025.
Amazon employees criticised the policy in internal messages and some said they were looking for new jobs.
